blocks.text: For the past five years, Stephan Vanfleteren (1969), an internationally renowned photographer, has maintained an almost obsessive relationship with the sea. A profound fascination at once compelling and dangerous has led him to explore this ever-changing, elusive and unpredictable world. With *Transcripts of a Sea* , he offers a personal interpretation of the sea, captured in all its diversity, through its moods, movements and shifting light.

Whether stormy or as calm as a mirror, shrouded in mist, swept by a storm, deceptively peaceful or churning like the drum of a washing machine, the sea is constantly transforming before his eyes. But Stephan Vanfleteren does not observe it from the shore or from the deck of a boat. He chooses direct, physical and sensory engagement: he literally steps into the water, immerses himself in this element and allows himself to be carried along by its power.

First presented to the public in September 2025 at the Museum of Fine Arts in Ghent (MSK), Transcripts of a Sea was an immediate and remarkable success, attracting over 140,000 visitors. Since then, the exhibition has continued its international tour. It is currently on display at the Maritime Museum in Amsterdam, the Netherlands, where it will remain open until April 2027.
Perhaps we should leave the appreciation to an expert:

(Stephan Vanfleteren is) A navigator without a boat, Stephan Vanfleteren seems to have adopted the castaway’s point of view. His body, held upright according to a performative protocol, finds its origins in a childhood memory: an accident involving near-drowning, whose outcome was ultimately a fortunate one. A rescue, like a second birth, that must be relived… Between each image, one must draw breath anew.
Do not look for the line of horizon. What you perceive is, more often than not, a waterline.

The horizon itself has been cast into invisibility. All that matters now is the supple blade of a receding swell, the splash of an exhausted wave at the height of its flight, the black liquor of nocturnal water. These formless substances are not landscapes. In Transcripts of a Sea, the figure of the castaway is one and the same as the element in which he is immersed, with which he has become indivisible.

Transcripts of a Sea is the outcome of an experience of being alive: of imagining oneself alive in the very place where one has felt one’s own death. Above all, it is the living that draws the great category of the “elements” (water, earth, fire) out of the metaphysical realm and inscribes it within an ecological sensibility. At first glance, the universality of these “transcriptions” asserts itself like a rising tide. Transcripts of a Sea is an immense recording, measuring the pulse of life as it composes with the contours of the water and the operator’s blood pressure. The sea thus becomes a place for meditating on freedom, expressed through the choice to place oneself in danger.
Michel Poivert Professor of the History of Photography
TRANSCRIPTS OF A SEA – art book – edition of Hannibal Books
And again we present the impressive art book.

The cover is based on the notebooks he uses trip after trip to entrust his notes to. When you pick up the book, you think you are holding an oversized Leuchtturm or Moleskine, with a hard cover, rounded corners, dog-eared, water-stained, faded… and somewhere a date, a date that Stephan Vanfleteren will never forget. The cover is like a palimpsest, with layers shining through.
The book contains 136 photographs by Stephan Vanfleteren, showing the sea in all its colours and overwhelming power. Highly recommended for all lovers of the sea…
